:::{#thm-newton-quadratic}
#### Newton's method minimizes a quadratic in one step

Let $\matr{S}$ be a $p \times p$ [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite) matrix,
$\vecf{c} \in \reals^p$,
and $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx - \tp{\vecf{c}} \vx$.
From any $\vx^{(0)}$, Newton's method (@def-newton-method) gives $\vx^{(1)} = \matr{S}^{-1} \vecf{c}$,
the unique minimizer of $f$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-quadratic-form and @cor-deriv-lincom-tp,
$\deriv{\vx} f(\vx) = \matr{S} \vx - \vecf{c}$;
by @thm-hessian-quadratic with $\tfrac{1}{2} \matr{S}$ in place of $\matr{S}$,
and because the gradient $-\vecf{c}$ of the linear term is constant (@def-constant-wrt-vector),
$\matr{H}_f(\vx) = \matr{S}$,
which is invertible ([positive definite inverse](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-pd-inverse)). So

$$
\ba
\vx^{(1)}
&= \vx^{(0)} - \matr{S}^{-1} (\matr{S} \vx^{(0)} - \vecf{c})
&& \text{(definition of Newton's method)}
\\
&= \vx^{(0)} - \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{S} \vx^{(0)} + \matr{S}^{-1} \vecf{c}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= \matr{S}^{-1} \vecf{c}.
&& \text{(} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{S} = \matr{I}_p \text{; cancel)}
\ea
$$

The gradient at $\matr{S}^{-1} \vecf{c}$ is $\matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} \vecf{c} - \vecf{c} = \vzero_{p \times 1}$,
and $f$ is strictly convex (@thm-convex-hessian, part 2),
so $\matr{S}^{-1} \vecf{c}$ is a global minimizer (@cor-convex-stationary).
It is the only one: a strictly convex function has at most one minimizer,
since the midpoint of two minimizers would have a strictly smaller value (@def-strictly-convex).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-newton-quadratic}
#### One step to the minimizer

Let $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2} (x_1^2 + 3 x_2^2)$, so $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 }$ and $\vecf{c} = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$.
From $\vx^{(0)} = \tp{(3, 1)}$ the gradient is $\tp{(3, 3)}$ and $\matr{S}^{-1} = \sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/3 }$, so
$\vx^{(1)} = \tp{(3, 1)} - \tp{(3, 1)} = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$, the minimizer.

:::
